result:
If I could change one thing, I think I'd want people to have an easier time extending good faith to each other—especially across disagreement.

So much friction in the world seems to come from assuming the worst about people whose views or circumstances differ from our own. It shows up in arguments where both sides feel certain the other is acting in bad faith, in political polarization, in how people treat strangers versus those in their own circle. A lot of cruelty seems to come not from malice but from failures of imagination about other people's inner lives.

I don't think this would solve everything—there are real conflicts of interest and genuine harms that good faith alone can't fix. But I suspect a lot of suffering is downstream of unnecessary suspicion and contempt, the kind that makes compromise feel like defeat and makes people talk past each other instead of with each other.

I'll admit there's something almost too neat about this answer, like the kind of thing that sounds wise without committing to anything specific. What draws you to the question? I'm curious whether you're thinking about this on a global scale or something closer to home.
